docs.title: An everest-optimizers plugin for ropt
docs.text: The ropt-eo package extends the ropt module by providing the Dakota-compatible optpp_q_newton method from the everest-optimizers package. ropt itself is a robust optimization framework designed for both continuous and discrete optimization workflows and is extensible through its plugin architecture. Installing ropt-eo makes this method available as eo/optpp_q_newton within ropt.

docs.title: ropt_eo.everest_optimizers.EverestOptimizers
docs.text:
Bases: Backend

OPT++ optimization backend for ropt.

This class provides the optpp_q_newton method of everest-optimizers, a replacement for the Dakota method of the same name. Like Dakota, it runs an interior-point method if there are linear or nonlinear constraints, a bound-constrained quasi-Newton method if there are finite bounds, and an unconstrained quasi-Newton or limited-memory BFGS method otherwise.

This backend cannot run concurrently in-process

OPT++ always creates an output file under a fixed name in the current working directory, which everest-optimizers deletes again once the run has started. Two runs at once in the same process therefore create and delete the same file, and each one's output_file is a path they share. To use this backend alongside anything else, prefix the method with external/ and it runs in a process of its own, through the external backend.

To select the optimizer, set the method field within the backend section of the EnOptContext configuration object to eo/optpp_q_newton or eo/default. For algorithm-specific options, use the options field within the backend section. It is either a dictionary keyed by option name, or a list of strings in the format of the Dakota optpp_q_newton method, such as ["search_method = trust_region", "max_step 10"]. Both forms accept the same options:

Method-specific Options:

Method Options optpp_q_newton search_method, merit_function, steplength_to_boundary, centering_parameter, max_step, gradient_tolerance, max_iterations, convergence_tolerance, max_function_evaluations, output, output_file

The tr_pds search method is not supported.

The output_file option is not a Dakota option: it names the file that receives the OPT++ output.

Some fields of the backend section set options as well:

  • max_iterations and convergence_tolerance replace the options of the same name.
  • verbose adds output debug, unless the options contain an output keyword. OPT++ is silent at all other output levels.
  • An evaluation_policy of speculative in the gradient section adds the Dakota speculative keyword.
